prerequisites: Read the symbols in this example

tutorNotes.observe: Ask the student to describe what changed before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why do we work out 2 + 3 first?

steps.title: Look inside the brackets
steps.explanation: The brackets group 2 + 3 together.
steps.detail: Work out this group before multiplying.

steps.title: Brackets come first
steps.explanation: First, focus on 2 + 3.
steps.detail: Keep the 6 and the multiplication sign where they are.

steps.title: Work out the group
steps.explanation: 2 + 3 = 5. Replace the bracketed group with 5.
steps.detail: The value of the group stays the same.

steps.title: Now multiply
steps.explanation: We now have 6 × 5.
steps.detail: That means six groups of five.

notation.spoken: 6 times open bracket 2 plus 3 close bracket

lessons.objective: Interpret signed arithmetic as controlled movement on a number line.
prerequisites: Read the symbols in this example

tutorNotes.observe: Ask the student to describe what changed before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Confusing the operation sign with the sign of the number.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Which direction did we move, and why?

steps.title: Start at the first number
steps.explanation: Start at 2 on the number line.

steps.title: Move left: 1 of 5
steps.explanation: Subtracting moves left. One step takes us to 1.

steps.title: Move left: 2 of 5
steps.explanation: Subtracting moves left. One step takes us to 0.

steps.title: Move left: 3 of 5
steps.explanation: Subtracting moves left. One step takes us to -1.
steps.detail: We have passed zero. Negative numbers are below zero.

steps.title: Move left: 4 of 5
steps.explanation: Subtracting moves left. One step takes us to -2.
steps.detail: We have passed zero. Negative numbers are below zero.

steps.title: Move left: 5 of 5
steps.explanation: Subtracting moves left. One step takes us to -3.
steps.detail: We have passed zero. Negative numbers are below zero.

steps.title: The answer is -3
steps.explanation: Five steps left from 2 reach −3.

lessons.objective: Interpret signed arithmetic as controlled movement on a number line.
prerequisites: Read the symbols in this example

tutorNotes.observe: Ask the student to describe what changed before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Confusing the operation sign with the sign of the number.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Which direction did we move, and why?

steps.title: Start at the first number

left.spoken: 4 plus open bracket minus 3 close bracket

steps.explanation: Start at 4 on the number line.

steps.title: Move left: 1 of 3

left.spoken: 4 plus open bracket minus 3 close bracket

steps.explanation: Adding a negative moves left. One step takes us to 3.

steps.title: Move left: 2 of 3

left.spoken: 4 plus open bracket minus 3 close bracket

steps.explanation: Adding a negative moves left. One step takes us to 2.

steps.title: Move left: 3 of 3

left.spoken: 4 plus open bracket minus 3 close bracket

steps.explanation: Adding a negative moves left. One step takes us to 1.

steps.title: The answer is 1

left.spoken: 4 plus open bracket minus 3 close bracket equals 1

steps.explanation: The + tells us to add; −3 is the number being added. Three steps left from 4 reach 1.

notation.spoken: 4 plus open bracket minus 3 close bracket

lessons.objective: Multiply before adding when there are no brackets.
prerequisites: Read the symbols in this example

tutorNotes.observe: Ask the student to describe what changed before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Which operation must we do before adding?

steps.title: Look at the two operations
steps.explanation: There is addition and multiplication. Multiplication comes first.

steps.title: Focus on multiplication
steps.explanation: Work out 3 × 2 before adding 4.

steps.title: Replace the product with six
steps.explanation: 3 × 2 is 6. Now we have 4 + 6.

lessons.objective: See that equal fractions shade the same amount of the same whole.
prerequisites: Read the symbols in this example

tutorNotes.observe: Ask the student to describe what changed before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Thinking a larger denominator means a larger shaded amount.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Did the shaded amount change when we added the dividing lines?

steps.title: Shade half of one whole
steps.explanation: The whole is split into two equal parts. One part is shaded.

steps.title: Split each half in two
steps.explanation: Divide each half into two equal parts. The shaded area stays the same.

steps.title: Compare the same sized wholes
steps.explanation: One of two parts is the same amount as two of four parts.

lessons.title: Three quarters of 20
lessons.label: Three quarters of 20
lessons.objective: Divide a quantity by the denominator, then select the numerator of equal groups.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Dividing by the numerator instead of making denominator-many equal groups.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why do we make four equal groups before selecting three?

steps.title: Start with twenty
steps.explanation: We want three of four equal parts of twenty counters.

steps.title: Split into four equal parts

left.text: twenty divided by four equals five
left.spoken: twenty divided by four equals five

steps.explanation: Four equal groups give five counters in each quarter.

scene.description: Four equal quarters, each with five counters.

steps.title: Select three of the four quarters
steps.explanation: Select three groups of five. Three quarters of twenty is fifteen.

scene.description: Three of four quarters are highlighted; fifteen counters are selected.

lessons.title: 25% of 80
lessons.label: 25% of 80
lessons.objective: Connect twenty-five percent with one quarter of the original whole.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Treating twenty-five percent as twenty-five objects for every original amount.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why does the whole amount matter when finding twenty-five percent?

steps.title: Twenty-five percent is one quarter

left.text: twenty-five percent equals twenty-five hundredths equals one quarter
left.spoken: twenty-five percent equals twenty-five hundredths equals one quarter

steps.explanation: Percent means parts per hundred. Twenty-five of a hundred is one quarter.

scene.description: Four equal cards of value twenty represent the whole eighty.
scene.caption: Each card represents 20, not one unit.

steps.title: Split the whole into four equal parts

left.text: eighty divided by four equals twenty
left.spoken: eighty divided by four equals twenty

steps.explanation: Divide the whole eighty into four equal groups. Each quarter is twenty.

scene.description: Four equal parts each have value twenty.
scene.caption: Each card represents 20.

steps.title: Take one quarter

left.text: twenty-five percent of eighty equals twenty
left.spoken: twenty-five percent of eighty equals twenty

steps.explanation: Select one of the four equal parts. Twenty-five percent of eighty is twenty.

scene.description: One quarter of the whole eighty is selected: twenty.
scene.caption: Each card represents 20.

lessons.title: Add equal-denominator fractions
lessons.label: Add equal-denominator fractions
lessons.objective: Count equal fractional units while keeping the whole fixed.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Adding denominators and changing the size of the fractional unit.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why does the denominator stay six when we add sixths?

steps.title: Six equal parts make one whole
steps.explanation: Each card stands for one sixth of the same whole. There are six equal parts.

scene.description: Six equal cards represent the six sixths of one whole.
scene.caption: Each card is one sixth of this whole.

steps.title: Select the first sixth
steps.explanation: Select one of the six equal parts.

scene.description: One of six equal parts is highlighted.
scene.caption: Each card is one sixth of this whole.

steps.title: Add two more sixths

left.text: one sixth plus two sixths equals three sixths
left.spoken: one sixth plus two sixths equals three sixths

steps.explanation: Add two more parts of the same size. Three sixths are now selected; the whole still has six parts.

scene.description: Three of six equal parts are highlighted.
scene.caption: Each card is one sixth of this whole.

steps.title: Three sixths is half
steps.explanation: Three of six equal parts cover half the whole. The denominator was not added.

scene.description: Exactly half of the six parts are highlighted.
scene.caption: Each card is one sixth of this whole.
